cues.text: Did you make notes while you were watching the performances of Romeo and Juliet, Gemma?
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: Yes, I did. I found it quite hard though.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: I kept getting too involved in the play.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: Me too. I ended up not taking notes.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: I wrote down my impressions when I got home.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: Do you mind if I check a few things with you?
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: In case I've missed anything.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: And I've also got some questions about our assignment.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: No, it's good to talk things through.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: I may have missed things too.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: OK great. So first of all, I'm not sure how much information we should include in our reviews.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: Right. Well, I don't think we need to describe what happens.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: Especially as Romeo and Juliet is one of Shakespeare's most well-known plays.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: Yeah, everyone knows the story.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: In an essay we'd focus on the poetry and Shakespeare's use of imagery etc., but that isn't really relevant in a review.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: We're supposed to focus on how effective this particular production is.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: Mmm. We should say what made it a success or a failure.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: And part of that means talking about the emotional impact the performance had on us.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: I think that's important.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: Yes. And we should definitely mention how well the director handled important bits of the play-like when Romeo climbs onto Juliet's balcony.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: And the fight between Mercutio and Tybalt.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: Yes. It would also be interesting to mention the theatre space and how the director used it but I don't think we'll have space in 800 words.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: No. OK. That all sounds quite straightforward.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: So what about The Emporium Theatre's production of the play?
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: I thought some things worked really well but there were some problems too.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: Yeah. What about the set, for example?
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: I think it was visually really stunning.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: I'd say that was probably the most memorable thing about this production.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: You're right.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: The set design was really amazing, but actually I have seen similar ideas used in other productions.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: What about the lighting?
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: Some of the scenes were so dimly lit it was quite hard to see.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: I didn't dislike it.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: It helped to change the mood of the quieter scenes.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: That's a good point.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: What did you think of the costumes?
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: I was a bit surprised by the contemporary dress, I must say.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: Yeah - I think it worked well, but I had assumed it would be more conventional.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: Me too. I liked the music at the beginning and I thought the musicians were brilliant, but I thought they were wasted because the music didn't have much impact in Acts 2 and 3.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: Yes - that was a shame.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: One problem with this production was that the actors didn't deliver the lines that well.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: They were speaking too fast.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: It was a problem I agree, but I thought it was because they weren't speaking loudly enough - especially at key points in the play.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: I actually didn't have a problem with that.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: It's been an interesting experience watching different versions of Romeo and Juliet, hasn't it?
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: Definitely. It's made me realise how relevant the play still is.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: Right. I mean a lot's changed since Shakespeare's time, but in many ways nothing's changed.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: There are always disagreements and tension between teenagers and their parents.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: Yes, that's something all young people can relate to - more than the violence and the extreme emotions in the play.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: How did you find watching it in translation?
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: Really interesting.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: I expected to find it more challenging, but I could follow the story pretty well.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: I stopped worrying about not being able to understand all the words and focused on the actors' expressions.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: The ending was pretty powerful.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: Yes. That somehow intensified the emotion for me.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: Did you know Shakespeare's been translated into more languages than any other writer?
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: What's the reason for his international appeal, do you think?
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: I was reading that it's because his plays are about basic themes that people everywhere are familiar with.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: Yeah, and they can also be understood on different levels.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: The characters have such depth.
cues.speaker: GEMMA

cues.text: Right - which allows directors to experiment and find new angles.
cues.speaker: ED

cues.text: That's really important because ...
cues.speaker: GEMMA
